How do you check a dentist's Turkish Dental Association (TDB) and specialty credentials?

Ask the clinic for the full name and diploma registration number of the specific dentist treating you—not just the clinic founder—then check their membership on the Turkish Dental Association (TDB) directory and verify the clinic's Ministry of Health International Health Tourism Authorization Certificate before paying any deposit.

Every licensed dentist in Türkiye must graduate from a recognized five-year dental faculty and register with their provincial chamber under the [Turkish Dental Association (TDB)](https://tdb.org.tr/dishekimi-bul). Separately, any clinic legally treating international patients must appear on the [Turkish Ministry of Health's register of authorized health tourism providers](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-69289/healthcare-providers-with-international-health-tourism-authorization-certificates.html) under the [Regulation on International Health Tourism](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-108974/regulation-on-international-health-tourism-and-tourist-health.html). The [UK General Dental Council (GDC)](https://www.gdc-uk.org/standards-guidance/information-for-patients-public/going-abroad-for-dental-treatment) likewise urges patients to confirm whether a practitioner who claims specialist status actually holds a recognized specialist qualification.
What is the difference between a general dentist, oral surgeon and prosthodontist?

A general dentist (Diş Hekimi) completes a five-year dental degree and handles routine restorative care. An oral and maxillofacial surgeon (Ağız, Diş ve Çene Cerrahı) and a prosthodontist (Protetik Diş Tedavisi Uzmanı) complete three to five additional years of state-recognized specialty residency (Uzmanlık or PhD) for complex surgical and bite-reconstruction cases.

What sterilization and 3D CBCT imaging standards should a clinic show?

A properly equipped dental clinic should use EN 13060 Class B pre-vacuum autoclaves with sealed, date-stamped instrument pouches, biological spore-test logs, and an in-house 3D Cone Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT) scanner for implant planning rather than relying solely on flat 2D panoramic X-rays.

Under European standard [EN 13060, Class B autoclaves](https://tuttnauer.com/blog/autoclave-sterilization/class-b-tabletop-autoclaves) use fractional vacuum pulses to remove trapped air, making them the required benchmark for sterilizing wrapped surgical kits and hollow handpieces. For implant surgery, a [clinical review on PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11276053/) confirms that 3D CBCT imaging maps bone width, bone density, sinus floors, and nerve canals in three dimensions—details a flat 2D X-ray cannot measure accurately. Ask to see the sterilization room during your in-person consultation; reputable clinics welcome transparency.
What written treatment plan must you receive before travelling?

Before booking flights, you should receive a written, itemized preliminary treatment plan naming your treating dentist, exact tooth numbers, specific implant and ceramic brands, expected visit counts, contingency costs for root canals or grafts, and full warranty conditions—clearly stating that final confirmation depends on your in-person 3D scan.
Verify your pre-travel paperwork against this checklist:

Clinic's Turkish Ministry of Health International Health Tourism Authorization Certificate number
Tooth-by-tooth breakdown specifying exact material brands (see our [zirconia vs E-max guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/zirconia-vs-emax-turkey))
Realistic day-by-day appointment and lab schedule (cross-check with our [dental trip duration guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/how-long-dental-trip-turkey))
Itemized pricing for potential clinical additions (extractions, root canals, bone grafts, nightguards)
Complete written warranty terms and exclusions (see our [Turkish dental warranty guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/dental-warranty-turkey))

faq.q: How can I check if a Turkish dental clinic is legally allowed to treat foreign patients?
faq.a: Ask for its Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Health International Health Tourism Authorization Certificate number and verify that the facility is listed on the Ministry's official authorized providers directory.

faq.q: Does TDB registration guarantee a dentist is a specialist?
faq.a: No. TDB registration confirms the dentist is legally licensed to practise in Türkiye. Specialist titles such as Oral Surgeon or Prosthodontist require additional postgraduate residency (Uzmanlık) or PhD credentials.

faq.q: Is a 2D panoramic X-ray enough to plan dental implants?
faq.a: A 2D panoramic X-ray works for an initial remote estimate, but safe surgical implant placement requires an in-person 3D CBCT scan to measure jawbone thickness, nerve pathways, and sinus boundaries.

faq.q: Why should I ask who my exact treating dentist will be before flying?
faq.a: Some high-volume clinics market a senior founder online while assigning international patients to junior associate dentists on arrival. Getting the treating clinician's name in writing prevents last-minute swaps.

faq.q: What should I do if a clinic refuses to share a written, itemized plan before I book?
faq.a: Treat that refusal as a warning sign. Reputable clinics provide a clear preliminary plan, brand names, and fee schedule before you commit to flights—while noting that final clinical decisions happen after in-person examination.
